title: A directional rule reduced the fixed-score detection threshold for four US ozone and warmth tests in 1995-2024
abstract: We compared three rules for a negative ozone by warmth interaction in all four US bird survey samples in 1995-2024. We used published aggregate state scores and a fixed symmetric state-sign error model. Removing the four-test correction reduced the 80 percent detection threshold from 1.370 to 1.113 recorded species. A one-sided conjunction reduced it further to 0.982. A conjunction needs no multiplicity correction if its marginal tests are valid. The observed conjunction p value was 0.728, so the common negative claim still failed. Exact western sign enumeration, marginal boundary checks and repeat calculations support the numeric comparison. The threshold is conditional on fixed estimated scores and errors. It is not real population power or a causal ecological effect. Observation bias, selected exposure coverage and common weather errors remain. Code, input hashes, aggregate evidence and repeat instructions are included.

display.caption: Three decision rules under fixed state-score errors. The observed data do not establish a common negative interaction.
